title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 104
paragraphs: The Milesians, too, had been appointed to guard the passes for the Persians, in order to secure their safety, so that if what actually came to pass should happen after all, they might have guides and so get safely away to the heights of Mycale. The Milesians, I say, had been appointed to do this, not only for that end but also from fear that, if they were present in the camp, they might make some hostile move. But they did in fact the opposite of what they were appointed to do; they not only directed the Persians in flight by wrong paths — by paths that led toward the enemy — but also at last themselves became their worst foes and began to slay them. Thus for the second time Ionia revolted from the Persians.
